To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucose induces accumulation of cAMP and insulin release in pancreatic islets and that these two processes are dependent on extracellular calcium.

the glucose effect on insulin release and cAMP accumulation in islets from ob/ob-mice are differentially sensitive to starvation and Ca++ and that the glucose-induced accumulation of cAMP may be mediated by a Ca++-independent process.
glucose-induced accumulation of cAMP is a Ca++-dependent process in the pancreatic islets of ob/ob mice that disappears after starvation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca++ in the glucose action on cAMP and insulin release from isolated pancreatic islets.
the study of glucose-induced insulin release in the pancreatic islet.
the effects of Ca++ and starvation on the cAMP system in the pancreatic islets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of glucose on the accumulation of cAMP differ markedly from the effects on insulin secretion and that this difference is due to the effects of starvation.
the glucose-induced accumulation of cAMP is a process that is Ca++-dependent, and that it differs from insulin secretion in that it is lost after 18 h starvation.
the glucose effect on cAMP is a phenomenon which can be studied in vitro, is dependent on Ca++, and which, in the mouse, is not a reflection of the physiological insulin secretion mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cAMP is involved in insulin release but is not an obligatory mediator of the process.
the cAMP accumulation in pancreatic islets is dependent on glucose, extracellular Ca++ and a functional beta cell membrane.
glucose-induced insulin release is not dependent on cAMP accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the effects of glucose on insulin release and cAMP accumulation in islets ofob/ob-mouse are very different and that the glucose-induced cAMP accumulation is a phenomenon which is not necessarily related to insulin release.
the cAMP system in islets is very sensitive to the nutritional state of the animal.
the glucose-induced accumulation of cAMP is a very sensitive indicator of the functional state of pancreatic islets.
